title: how to build (almost) anything with a magic computer
subtitle: bespoke software and intelligent systems for your problems and possibilities.
summary: learn how to work with ai to solve your problems and bring your visions to life. build bespoke software and intelligent systems shaped around the way you work.
introduction: work with ai to turn your problems, ideas, and ambitions into bespoke software and intelligent systems. learn how to give your assistant useful context, shape a practical plan, and build something that brings your vision to life — one reviewable step at a time.
audience: curious people, creatives, and small teams who want to make useful tools for their own work. you do not need to arrive as a software developer.
experience: start with a small, real problem
bring: a laptop and a project idea. supported tools, accounts, and any subscription requirements will be listed when a session opens.
outcomes: turn an idea into a small, clear brief with a practical definition of done.
give claude or codex the context, examples, and constraints it needs.
build in reviewable steps, keep a recoverable history, and handle mistakes.
check behaviour with real examples and understand what needs attention before sharing a tool.

outline.title: find the useful little thing
outline.text: choose a manageable problem. describe who the tool is for, what it should do, and what it can leave out.

outline.title: brief your assistant
outline.text: supply context, representative data, constraints, and examples. make the plan concrete before building.

outline.title: build, inspect, repeat
outline.text: work in small steps. read the result, try it yourself, and keep a way back when something breaks.

outline.title: make it usable
outline.text: test the awkward cases. think through private data, permissions, costs, and how you will maintain the thing you made.

title: creative ai: material, not magic
subtitle: a practical introduction to making with generative ai.
summary: get beyond the default output. understand how generative tools work, explore their ethical fault lines, and learn to direct them with your own creative intent.
introduction: a hands-on introduction that starts with how the systems work and ends with your own experiment. move from a reference or sketch to a more deliberate result, while keeping the human decisions in view.
audience: artists, designers, educators, students, and curious beginners looking for a grounded introduction to creative ai.
bring: a creative idea, sketch, or photograph you have permission to use. laptop and account requirements will be confirmed before booking.
outcomes: explain the basic relationship between training data, prompts, and generated output.
recognise questions of bias, mimicry, authorship, and personal boundaries.
use references and a repeatable calibration process to direct a creative experiment.
record your decisions so you can explain what you contributed to the result.

outline.title: under the hood
outline.text: a plain-language introduction to generative systems, with examples across creative media.

outline.title: ethics and boundaries
outline.text: discuss whose work goes into the tools, what comes out, and where you want to draw your own lines.

outline.title: from default to directed
outline.text: compare an uncalibrated output with a deliberate experiment using your own reference, vocabulary, and constraints.

outline.title: show your working
outline.text: share what happened, what you changed, and which decisions mattered. the process is part of the work.

idea_heading: make room for your own practice.

title: provocations
subtitle: an intensive 8-week studio for artists in a world of ai.
summary: an intensive 8-week course and studio for artists. work through weekly provocations, make and question your own work, and develop a creative practice with ai as a material. sceptics welcome.
introduction: an intensive 8-week studio for artists who want to understand the tools, test their limits, and decide what belongs in their practice. start with the mechanics, develop work through weekly provocations and shared critique, and make your own case for what is worth exhibiting — or refusing.
audience: practising and emerging artists, designers, and creative people who want room to experiment and think critically.
bring: your own creative questions and material to work with. equipment and account requirements will be confirmed with each session.
outcomes: understand the mechanics behind generative tools and how they shape the work.
build a personal reference library and explore how different platforms respond.
make your choices, labour, and creative intent visible through a process journal.
develop your own position on authorship, mimicry, and when to refuse a tool.

outline.title: week 1 // material, not magic
outline.text: a technical deep-dive into training data, models, prompts, and reference libraries. open up the mechanics and the ethical questions that will shape your studio practice.

outline.title: weeks 2–7 // guided studio
outline.text: respond to weekly provocations: the glossiest slop on earth, mimesis, make the effort legible, aura & context, edges & refusals, and indefense of ai. make work, share your process, and develop it through critical conversation.

outline.title: week 8 // ai art sucks
outline.text: bring your work and your position to a final collective critique. decide what deserves to be exhibited, what needs more work, and what you would rather leave unmade.

idea_heading: eight weeks for your own practice.

title: agent overlord
subtitle: build agentic systems for the way you live and work.
summary: a course for people who want to set up agentic systems in their life. design useful agents, give them clear boundaries, and build workflows you can understand, supervise, and improve.
introduction: go beyond a single conversation with an ai assistant. learn how to design agentic systems around real parts of your life: deciding what to delegate, connecting the right tools, keeping control of permissions, and checking that the system does what you intended.
audience: curious people, creatives, and small teams ready to invest time in building and supervising their own agentic systems.
experience: bring a workflow you want to improve
bring: a laptop and a real workflow to explore. the course length, supported tools, and account requirements will be confirmed before bookings open.
outcomes: identify tasks worth delegating and decide what should stay under your control.
design clear roles, instructions, and boundaries for your agents.
connect tools and information with deliberate permissions and a way to recover.
evaluate an agentic workflow, inspect failures, and improve it over time.

outline.title: find the right jobs
outline.text: map the repeated work in your life and choose a useful, manageable place to start.

outline.title: design the system
outline.text: define agent roles, the context they need, and when they should ask you for a decision.

outline.title: connect and supervise
outline.text: bring tools into the workflow with clear permissions, visible actions, and practical recovery points.

outline.title: test, live with it, improve it
outline.text: try real scenarios, examine failures, and develop a routine for checking and maintaining your system.
